name: unlimited-model-calls
text:
A document declares the model-call ceiling of a budget as unlimited by writing
the string `"unlimited"`.

A contract declares no wall-clock limit, no input-token limit, and no
output-token limit by leaving each key out. It has no way to declare the same
for model calls: the `model_calls` field of a `budget` block
(`crates/contract/src/document.rs`) is a plain integer, so the only way to run
without a ceiling is to name a number large enough never to be reached, and a
number above 2^53 loses precision in every JSON reader that holds it as a
double.

Make `model_calls` a number or the string `"unlimited"`, with the resolved
value an `Option<u64>`, as for the three dimensions that mean unlimited by
absence. The field stays required: a document states what it allows, and
cannot become unbounded by leaving a key out. A string other than `"unlimited"`
is refused, and the refusal contains the words `expected a number or "unlimited"`.
The wire form carries the same word, so a log records an unbounded episode with
it.

`foe plan` prints "no model-call limit" for it, and the Python package
accepts and validates the same two forms.

The documents under docs/ describe the behavior. Each sentence below belongs in the document named before it, in the same words:
- docs/config.md: "unlimited" declares no ceiling on this dimension.
- docs/config.md: the field is required either way, so a document states what it allows and does not become unbounded by leaving one out
- docs/log-format.md: model_calls is a number or the string "unlimited", which records that the episode enforces no ceiling on model requests; the other three spend dimensions record the same thing by absence.

checks/run.sh runs the checks this task is judged on: the tests of foe, foe-contract, foe-core, foe-log, foe-team, foe-workflow, clippy with warnings denied on the same crates, and scripts/loc.sh.

Follow AGENTS.md. Run the checks it names. When you finish, or when you cannot, report your outcome.
